 JUDGMENT
The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the death of Channakeshava B.H., in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners' case are as under:
2. That on 8.4.2023 at about 9.00 p.m. deceased Channakeshava B.H. was proceeding in a motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-HN-4872 as a pillion rider from Yadiyur side on Bengaluru- Mangaluru road, when they reached near Taj Hotel, KRS Agrahara, Kunigal Town, suddenly, rider of motor cycle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, at that point of time, one street dog suddenly came across the Honda Activa, the rider of the said vehicle suddenly applied break of his vehicle. Due to the sudden impact Channakeshava was thrown up and fell down on the left side of the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to CHC Kunigal Hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to A.C. Giri Hospital, Belluru, he was referred to higher hospital,
again he was shifted to Indian Health Hospital, Bengaluru, from there to Victoria Hospital,
Bengaluru, inspite of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 18.4.2023.
Thereafter, post mortem was conducted and the body was handed over to the petitioners.
The petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, transportation of dead body, funeral, obsequies ceremonies and other incidental expenses.

3. It is further stated that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, aged about 48 years, doing business and earning Rs.2,500/- to Rs.3,500/- per day and contributing entire income towards the welfare of the family.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, life of the petitioners become dark, miserable and put to great financial hardship.
4. It is contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-HN-4872.
In this regard, Kunigal Police have registered the case against the rider of the said vehicle in Crime No.38/2023.
As such, the respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.

sentences.text: In response to the notice, respondents have appeared through their respective counsel the respondent No.2 has filed the written statement, on the other hand the respondent No.1 has not filed her written statement.
6. In the written statement, the respondent No.2 contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further, this respondent has admitted about issuance of insurance policy in respect of motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06- HN-4872 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It is also contention of the respondent No.2 that, the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective D.L. as on the date of the accident.

It is the defence of the respondent No.2 that the accident occurred due to negligence on the part of the deceased himself and not on the part of the rider of offending vehicle as the deceased by consuming alcohol riding the vehicle without wearing helmet.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship between deceased with the petitioners.
Ultimately contended that the claim of the petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and arbitrary.

With all these main grounds,
prayed to dismiss the petition against this respondent.

7. On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, this tribunal has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioners proves that Channakeshava B.H., died due to the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 8.4.2023 at about 9.00 p.m. infront of Taj Hotel, KRS Agrahara on Kunigal town,
Benglauru-Mangaluru road, due to the rash and engligent riding of the rider of the Honda Activa bearing registration No.KA-06-HN-4872 in an actionable negligence ?
2. Whether the petitioenrs prove that they are the legal heirs and were depending upon the income of the decased?
3. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
from whom?
4. What order or award?
8. In order to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P19.

In addition to that, the petitioners got examined one eye witness as PW2.
9.
On the other hand, respondent No.2 has not led any rebuttal evidence on its behalf.

10. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
11.
My findings to the above issues as follows:

As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S  ISSUE No.1:-
12.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.8.4.2023, alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, Channakeshava B.H. had died.
As such, the petitioners being the legal heirs of the deceased have filed the claim petition for consideration.

13. On the other hand, the respondent No.2 contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased and not on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-HN-4872.
14.

On the basis of rival contention of both the parties, first of all, the petitioners have to place satisfactory evidence on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities against the rider of the offending vehicle in question.
15. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 by name Dilip Kumar got examined as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.

The petitioner in support of his oral evidence has relied upon the police documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P7, Ex.P12 & Ex.P13.
16.
On going through the documents, Ex.P1- true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No118/2023 of Kunigal Police Station.

Ex.P2-true copy of the first information statement given by Dhanush Kumar,
Ex.P3-true copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P4- true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5-true copy of PM report,
Ex.P6- true copy inquest report, Ex.P7-true copy of IMV report, Ex.P12-true copy of vehicle inspection mahazar and Ex.P13-true copy of charge sheet.

17. On perusal of the police documents it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Dhanush Kumar, the S.H.O. of Kunigal P.S. have registered the case against the rider of motor cycle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of IPC.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against rider of the motor cycle vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 & 304(A) of IPC.
18.
Apart from this, the petitioner examined one eye witness as PW2.
He has supported the version of the petitioner.

sentences.text: On the other hand, though the respondent No.2 has taken contention that the accident was not occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle, but not made an effort to examine either the rider of the offending vehicle or any of the independent eye witness to prove its contention.

20. PW1 & PW2 were subjected for cross- examination, but no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondents about the denial of allegation made against the rider of the offending vehicle.
21. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioners, I am of the view that, the petitioners have placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-06-HN-4872 and in the said accident, Channakeshava B.H. succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No. 2 & 3:
22.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which, the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account of the death of a person, due to a motor vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Since in the death case,
the legal heirs are the claimants.
In the case on hand, the relationship of deceased with the petitioners is not in dispute.

At the same time, the documents produced by the petitioners, to prove their relationship with the deceased marked at Ex.P8 to Ex.P11 & Ex.P14 i.e., Aadhar cards of the deceased and the petitioner No.1 to 3 and ration card, have not been disputed by the other side.
The recitals of the above documents clearly speak about the relationship between the petitioners and the deceased.

23. Another aspect to be considered herein that, on going through the particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition reflected that, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are children of the deceased have lost their love and affection of their father and the petitioner No.3 being the mother of the deceased has lost love and affection of her son, who was the backbone of the family.
Hence, it is crystal clear that, the petitioners were dependents on the deceased during his lifetime.
24. In the case on hand, no doubt the major children and mother of deceased-Channakeshava have filed this claim petition.
According to them, the petitioner No.1 & 2 were dependents to the deceased during his lifetime.
No contra materials are available on record to show that, they were not dependents to their father during his lifetime.
Here, it is necessary discuss the point that, father place an important role in the family.
All the children, one or the other way defendants to their parents whether they are minors or majors, married or unmarried.
But the percentage of disability may be varied from one person to another person.
During the minority of the child, dependency is more on the parents.
After the marriage of the children, the percentage of disability is less on the parents, if compare with the minor children.

sentences.text: In the case on hand, by looking to the age criteria though the petitioner No.1 & 2 are major sons of the deceased, they could have dependents to their father, not only economically, but in connection with love and affection during his lifetime.
Hence, the petitioners can be presumed as dependents to their father during his lifetime in the absence of contra materials from the other side.
26. The Division Bench of Supreme Court, in National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others stated that, a major and earning son has a right to claim compensation under Motor Vehicle Act.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/S Birender and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In this case, by referring the case of Manjuri Bera, stated that, even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant if he was a legal representative will be entitled to compensation.

Even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation, and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application,
irrespective of the fact, whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."
27. The petitioners herein, have placed Aadhar card, which is marked at Ex.P8 to prove the actual age of the deceased as on the date of the accident.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the deceased has been mentioned as 1.1.1973.
The accident occurred on 8.4.2023.

Therefore,
as on the date of accident, the deceased was aged about 50 years. For his age, multiplier '13' is applicable as per the ratio in "Sarala Verma"
Case.
28.

In connection with the work of the deceased, in the main petition and also in the evidence of PW1 stated that, deceased was doing wholesale fish selling business and was earning Rs.2,500/- to Rs.3,500/- per day.
The petitioners have not placed any documents to show the income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
It is pertinent to note that, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.

By keeping in mind about the year of the accident and also notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/-
for the year 2023.
29.
Apart from this, it is also relevant to discuss, that the Honourable Supreme Court in the decision reported in, 2018 SAR (Civil) 81.

National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The addition should be 30 per cent, if the age of the deceased was between 40 and 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 and 60 years, the addition should be 15 per cent.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was self-employed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 per cent of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 year.
An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years.

An addition of 25 per cent where the deceased Dilip Kumar vs Mangalamma on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199760859/
6 was between the age of 40 and 50 years and 10 per cent where the deceased was between the age of 50-60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.

entities.text: Dilip Kumar vs Mangalamma on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
30.

Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
31. In the light of the above proposition, in the case on hand, there are three persons were depending upon the income of the deceased.
Hence, as per the principle laid down by the Honourable Supreme Court in Sarala Verma Case at para No.14, 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses out of the total compensation.
32. In the present case, deceased was aged about 50 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "13" is applicable.

And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of 50-60 years, 10% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Therefore, by considering the earning of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
Along with this, the future prospects of 10% is to be taken in to consideration, then the annual income of the deceased comes to (Rs.1,92,000+19,200) = Rs.2,11,200/-.
And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.

Thus, net loss of income comes to Rs.1,40,800/-
(Rs.2,11,200-Rs.70,400).

This income has to be multiplied by multiplier "13" which comes to Rs.18,30,400/-.
33.

Apart from this aspect, in connection with the loss of estate, consortium and with respect to the funeral expenses to calculate the quantum of the compensation under the aforesaid heads, it is relevant to note herein the following authority;
2018 SAR (Civil) 81. National Insurance Company Limited.
V/ s Pranay Sethi and others, The Hon'ble Apex Court discussed various aspects in connection with the claim petition filed by the claimants for compensation.

And also observed that while determining the claim petition, the reasonable figures on conventional heads, viz., loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

34. By relying upon the above said decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, the amount of Rs.16,500/- is awarded under the head loss of estate and Rs.16,500/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and also by placing reliance upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in Dilip Kumar vs Mangalamma on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199760859/
7 (2018) 18 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited v/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram & Others, the amount of Rs.44,000/- each is awarded to the petitioner No.1 to 3 under the head loss of consortium.

sentences.text: Medical Expenses:

35. PW1 has stated in her evidence that immediately after the accident his father was shifted to CHC Kunigal Hospital, after first aid treatment he was shifted to A.C. Giri Hospital, Belluru, he was referred to higher hospital, against he was shifted to Indian Health Hospital, Bengaluru, from there to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, inspite of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 18.4.2023.
The petitioners have spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
To substantiate the said fact, the petitioners have placed outpatient record, attendant pass, prescriptions, medical bills and CT scan films, which are marked as Ex.P15 to Ex.P19.

On perusal of medical bills marked at Ex.P18 for Rs.48,094/-
along with prescriptions at Ex.P17.
There are no contra materials available on record to disprove the medical bills.
But on perusal of medical bills, Sl.No.9 of Rs.20,000/- is receipt for having paid the amount.
Hence, the said amount is not considered.
After deducting the said amount it comes to Rs.28,094/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.28,094/- towards medical expenses.
36. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation under the following heads.
Compensation heads Compensation

Amount  Towards loss of Rs.18,30,400-00  dependency  Towards loss of Rs. 1,32,000-00  consortium  Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500-00  Towards funeral & Rs. 16,500-00  obsequies ceremony  expenses  Medical expenses Rs. 28,094-00

Accordingly, the petitioners herein are entitled to get total compensation of Rs.20,23,494/-
(Rupees twenty lakhs twenty three thousand four hundred and ninety four only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Hon'ble High court of Dilip Kumar vs Mangalamma on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199760859/

LIABILITY:
38.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-06-HN-4872, alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioners in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.
owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
39. As per records insurance policy was valid from 28.7.2022 to 27.7.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 8.4.2023.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Hence, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition, till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 is Affirmative and the issue No.3 is Partly Affirmative.

ISSUE No.4:
40.

In view of my due discussions on Issue Nos.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following;
 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,23,494/- (Rupees twenty lakhs twenty three thousand four hundred and ninety four only ) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for the share of 40% each and the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 20%.

After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 2, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.3, since the award amount is very meagre, entire amount shall be released to her through due process of law.

Hence, in the absence of the definite income of the deceased, it is opt to consider the notional income as per law.
National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and others, " It was observed that, "While determining the income, an addition of 50 per cent of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where the deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years, should be made.
The established income means the income minus the tax component. "
30.
Having considered the above, as per law laid down in the above case, in connection with the deduction of personal and living expenses is concerned, it is settled that, "where the deceased was married, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased should be one third (1/3 rd) where the number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/4 th where the number of dependent family member is 4 to 6 and one fifth (1/5 th ) where the number of the dependent family members exceeds six."
32. In the present case, deceased was aged about 50 years as on the date of the accident.
For this age multiplier "13" is applicable.
And by relying on the aforesaid principle laid down in the Pranay Sethi's case with respect to the age of the deceased and also on going through the nature of the occupation forthcoming in the petition averments, it is evident that, the deceased herein is not having permanent job and accurate income for consideration.
As such, deceased was comes under the purview of 50-60 years, 10% income of the deceased has to be taken into account towards future prospects.
Annual income of the deceased was Rs.1,92,000/- per year.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C.
owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
39. As per records insurance policy was valid from 28.7.2022 to 27.7.2023.
The alleged accident had taken place on 8.4.2023.
As such, the respondent No.2 being the insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1.

And 1/3rd has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses in the income of the deceased.
The aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

 O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.20,23,494/- (Rupees twenty lakhs twenty three thousand four hundred and ninety four only ) from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for the share of 40% each and the petitioner No.3 is entitled the share of 20%.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.1 & 2, 40% of their share shall be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank of their choice for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% of their share shall be released in favour of them through due process of law.
After deposit of the compensation amount together with interest of petitioner No.3, since the award amount is very meagre, entire amount shall be released to her through due process of law.
